issues.legal_issue: A development scheme cannot include land outside municipal limits unless the authority validly frames an expansion scheme after forming the required opinion.
material_facts: The Trust framed and notified a scheme described as a development-cum-housing accommodation scheme.
The scheme included land both inside and outside the municipal limits.
The Trust’s resolutions and notice did not describe the scheme as an expansion scheme, and the Trust had not formed the opinion required for an expansion scheme.
issues.conclusion: The scheme could not be sustained as a development scheme covering land outside municipal limits or recharacterised as an expansion scheme, and was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 24(1) and 24(2) of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, a development scheme may cover a locality within municipal limits, while an expansion scheme for an adjacent locality requires the Trust to form the opinion specified in section 24(2). Section 25 provides for housing accommodation schemes, and section 28 permits schemes to combine types or features. The statutory powers are limited, not plenary, and the required opinion is a condition precedent to an expansion scheme.

rule.if: statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge and outside_municipal_land_included and scheme_described_as_development_or_housing and expansion_opinion_not_formed

predicates.statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a scheme prepared by a statutory improvement authority.
predicates.outside_municipal_land_included: The scheme includes land outside the municipality as well as land within it.
predicates.scheme_described_as_development_or_housi: The authority’s resolutions or notice describe the scheme as a development scheme, a housing accommodation scheme, or a combination of those schemes rather than as an expansion scheme.
predicates.expansion_opinion_not_formed: The authority did not form the opinion required before preparing a scheme for municipal expansion.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a statutory improvement scheme described as a development or housing scheme, includes land beyond municipal limits, and the authority did not form the required expansion opinion, the scheme is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An authority cannot save an act under a different statutory power when that power depends on a condition precedent that the authority did not satisfy.
material_facts: The Trust’s resolutions referred to statutory provisions concerning development and housing schemes and described the scheme in those terms.
The Trust had not formed the opinion required to prepare an expansion scheme.
The appellants relied on decisions allowing an act to stand despite a mistaken reference to the source of power.
issues.conclusion: The principle that a mistaken reference to a provision does not necessarily invalidate an act did not save this scheme, because the condition precedent for the asserted alternative power had not been satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: The Court recognised the principle that an act may remain valid if it can be supported by a lawful power despite a wrong reference to the provision authorising it. It distinguished L. Hazari Mal Kuthiala v. Income-tax Officer, Special Circle, Ambala Cantt. and Hukumchand Mills Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, because the alternative power here required the authority to form a particular opinion before acting; that opinion was a condition precedent.

rule.if: statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge and authority_relies_on_alternative_power and alternative_power_requires_prior_opinion and required_opinion_not_formed

predicates.statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge: A proceeding challenges an act taken in preparing a statutory improvement scheme.
predicates.authority_relies_on_alternative_power: The authority or a party seeks to support the act under a power different from the one under which the authority purported to act.
predicates.alternative_power_requires_prior_opinion: The alternative power is exercisable only after the authority forms a specified opinion.
predicates.required_opinion_not_formed: The authority did not form the specified opinion before taking the act.

issues.definition: If an authority seeks to rely on an alternative power that requires a prior opinion, but did not form that opinion, the alternative power cannot validate the act.

issues.legal_issue: Government sanction does not cure a scheme’s invalidity when the scheme was presented and approved as a different type of scheme.
material_facts: The Trust submitted the scheme to the Government as a development-cum-housing accommodation scheme.
The scheme included land outside municipal limits, and the Trust had not framed it as an expansion scheme or formed the opinion required for such a scheme.
issues.conclusion: Government sanction did not change the legal character of the scheme or cure its invalidity; the Court could not assume that the Government would have sanctioned an expansion scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 41 of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, schemes require Government sanction before coming into force. The Government must know the nature of the scheme to assess its necessity and feasibility. Approval of a scheme presented as one type does not establish that a different type would have been sanctioned or alter the statutory limits on the authority’s power.

rule.if: statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge and government_sanctioned_scheme and government_was_told_scheme_category and valid_scheme_required_different_category

predicates.statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a scheme prepared by a statutory improvement authority.
predicates.government_sanctioned_scheme: The Government approved the scheme submitted by the authority.
predicates.government_was_told_scheme_category: The authority informed the Government that the scheme belonged to a particular category.
predicates.valid_scheme_required_different_category: The scheme could have been valid only if it had been prepared under a different category of statutory power.

issues.definition: When the Government sanctions a scheme after being told it is of one category, that sanction does not cure invalidity if validity required preparation under a different category.

issues.legal_issue: An indivisible scheme that is partly invalid cannot be upheld in part and must stand or fall as a whole.
material_facts: The scheme combined development and housing purposes and covered land both within and outside municipal limits.
The Court found that the scheme was one and indivisible, rather than separable into independently valid and invalid parts.
issues.conclusion: The scheme could not be upheld in part and had to be set aside as a whole.
issues.legal_principle: Where a statutory scheme is one and indivisible, it cannot be treated as partly valid and partly invalid; it must stand or fall as a whole.

predicates.statutory_improvement_scheme_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a statutory improvement scheme.
predicates.scheme_is_indivisible: The scheme cannot be separated into distinct portions that can operate independently.
predicates.part_of_scheme_is_invalid: At least one part of the scheme is invalid.

issues.definition: If a challenged statutory improvement scheme is indivisible and part of it is invalid, the entire scheme is invalid.
